application.name: Color Convert
application.description: A synthetic camera's NV12 or YUYV frames converted to RGBA by holoscan-color-convert's ColorConvertOp and letterboxed by its ResizeOp in the same pass, shown by HoloViz in a window or rendered offscreen, with every output and render checked against the module's CPU reference.

changelog.1.0.0: Initial release: the holoscan-color-convert demo, with a synthetic NV12/YUYV camera, ColorConvertOp and ResizeOp on the cuda, vic or auto backend, a HoloViz window or offscreen render, and checks against the CPU reference.

hardware.name: NVIDIA GPU
hardware.description: A CUDA-capable GPU supported by the Holoscan SDK.

hardware.name: Display
hardware.description: For the window mode only; the offscreen and ci modes need none.

window.description: Live: 1920x1080 NV12 at 30 frames per second, converted to RGBA and shown in a HoloViz window with the 640x640 letterboxed resize inset, until the window is closed.

offscreen.description: HoloViz renders offscreen into CUDA memory: 60 frames, each output checked against the CPU reference and each render against its frame.

ci.description: Finite headless check: 60 YUYV and 1080p frames on the auto backend, every output checked against the CPU reference (byte for byte on CUDA, within tolerance on the VIC); on a CI runner, auto must take the VIC on the Jetson and CUDA on x86_64.
